title: Measurement Weighting Sets the GPS-Holdover Tolerance of PMU-Based Generator Dynamic State Estimation
content: Phasor measurement units (PMUs) lose GPS time and enter holdover on a local oscillator, whose drift rotates every reported phasor. How long holdover can last before generator dynamic state estimation degrades remains unquantified. We study an extended Kalman filter on the IEEE 39-bus system against an ANDES simulation with stochastic loads and field-level PMU noise, under a pre-specified analysis plan. We derive a closed form for the share of PMU phase drift reaching rotor-angle estimates; it matched all 21 tested cases within 3%. This share depends on the filter’s weighting of active power against voltage angle. With noise variances calibrated to the innovations, a drifting PMU passed up to 3.0 times its phase error into the rotor angles. With compensated quartz, the error reached 0.005 rad (0.29°) after 3.5–11 min, before the PMU’s own angle error (14.7 min). Weighting power more heavily cut the pass-through 13–32-fold at the simulated locations and had the lower no-drift error (2.4 against 3.2 mrad). A clock-aware filter removed drift at some cost in ambient accuracy; with power measurements, an innovation test detected every simulated single-PMU drift without holdover flags. Holdover tolerance depends on the estimator’s weighting as much as on the oscillator.
